# SiteVocal

> SiteVocal is a free, open-source, zero-API website-to-speech reader. Paste a company homepage (or click the extension on one) and it plays a 60-second Site Briefing of what the company does: who they are, what they provide, pricing and audience, and key FAQ. Summarize Page reads a few-minute summary of any whole page, section by section, and turns its tables, pricing grids, spec lists and bullet lists into short spoken sentences. For articles, it strips the ads and clutter with a 3-stage Ad-Shield, then reads the article aloud like a radio broadcast using the Web Speech API built into the browser (window.speechSynthesis), with a live teleprompter, a section outline, quote clipping, an Up Next queue and a resume library stored in localStorage. It runs as a web app (index.html with app.js and vendor/, no remote code) and, from the same folder, as a Manifest V3 Chrome extension whose side panel reads the active tab.

Key facts:

- Cost and licence: free, Apache-2.0. No API keys, accounts, servers or build step. Version 2.8.0.
- Data: SiteVocal collects no data. It has no server, no account and no analytics; everything it keeps (library, saved pages, clips, Up Next, dictionary, settings, optional Turbo keys) stays in the browser's localStorage, or the extension's own storage.
- New in 2.6:
  - "SiteVocal collects nothing: no account, no analytics, no tracking" on the start page, in the privacy panel and in a new Your data dialog (from the start page, the Library footer or the privacy panel).
  - Your data lists what is kept in this browser and how much space it takes, says which services can see a page's address or text, and has Clear everything (two taps; every sitevocal_* key, and in the extension the pending toolbar request and icon setting; nothing else on the site).
  - "Forget what I listened to when I close SiteVocal" erases the library, saved pages, clips, Up Next and stats whenever SiteVocal closes (tab, side panel, popup or studio tab); settings, the dictionary and keys stay. A one-time note under Continue listening points to Your data.
  - The extension asks for no site access at install: no host_permissions and no static content script; http://*/* and https://*/* are optional_host_permissions. Clicking SiteVocal on a tab reads it (activeTab). "Allow all sites" (tab card, error card, privacy panel, Your data) shows Chrome's prompt; then the side panel follows every tab, pasted links load straight from the browser and the right-click helper is registered. Without it, pasted links load like the web app. Turbo Engine services are asked for one host at a time (Test voice, or Allow in the notice).
  - Chrome Web Store compliance: without site access the extension asks once, in the loading card, before a public page service may fetch a link ("Not now" sends nothing); Allow all sites explains what changes before Chrome's prompt; nothing is prefetched on hover and no domain goes to Google's favicon service; Turbo endpoints must be https (http only on the user's own network); PRIVACY.md carries the Limited Use statement. Checked with webstore-lint (no findings), Chromium (no install-time permission warning), addons-linter, eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized, retire.js and the SchemaStore manifest schema.
- New in 2.5:
  - Predictive prefetch: a link starts loading when it is pasted into the start page or address pill, after 250 ms of no typing on a full address, or when the pointer rests 120 ms on a Quick Try, Up Next or Library item. Listen then opens it from an in-memory cache (10 pages, 5 minutes) in a few milliseconds, or attaches to the load in flight.
  - Two-tier race: the direct fetch and api.allorigins.win start at once. The keyless r.jina.ai reader joins only for an app shell (at once), after tier-1 failures, or at 220 ms, so fast server-rendered pages never reach it. With a TinyFish key, only TinyFish is asked, with keyless r.jina.ai as its fallback.
  - GitHub past the 60-an-hour API limit: READMEs from raw.githubusercontent.com (HEAD, then main, then master). Issues, pull requests and discussions (discussions always) come from the page itself: GitHub's HTML when it carries the thread, else r.jina.ai's rendering, with GitHub's chrome removed and every comment credited ("grace-h writes: …").
  - In the extension, a privileged fetch that returns an app shell goes straight to r.jina.ai in one hop.
  - The next sentence's utterance is prepared while the current one is spoken.
- Any link (new in 2.4): GitHub repositories, files (blob and raw.githubusercontent.com), issues and pull requests are read through GitHub's REST API (api.github.com, CORS-enabled, no key): the repository and its rendered README (Accept: application/vnd.github.html+json) are fetched in parallel, the owner's avatar is the logo, and the name, description, stars, forks, language, licence, topics and homepage open the page before the full README, whose tables are summarized. Past the 60-an-hour API limit the README comes from raw.githubusercontent.com. Other pasted URLs race a direct fetch and api.allorigins.win (raw and JSON); the keyless r.jina.ai reader joins only when needed (2.5), then api.codetabs.com (after 350 ms) and corsproxy.io (after 2.5 s). The first real page wins and the other requests are aborted. An app shell (Next.js, React; fewer than 200 readable characters) is replaced by r.jina.ai's rendered Markdown, converted back to headings, paragraphs, lists and tables. The address pill shows the stage: Connecting, Extracting DOM, Ready · N ms. Optional Jina or TinyFish keys raise r.jina.ai's keyless limit of 20 pages a minute.
- Summarize Page mode (new in 2.3): the third segment of the reader's mode bar ("Site Briefing | Full Page Read | Summarize Page"). After the Ad-Shield, the page is split at its H1 and every H2/H3; sentences are ranked by TF-IDF and TextRank keyword centrality, position and number/name density. Since 2.7 the summary is short: one line on what the page is, then 2 to 5 plain-language points from anywhere on the page in page order (no headings, captions, tech-tag lists or layout references), and one sentence for the pricing or main table; usually under a minute. Spoken as "Page Summary of [title], from [site]." … "That's the summary of [site]."
- Tables in Summarize Page and Site Briefing are never skipped, even with Skip Tables on: "Table Summary for Plans compared: Compares 3 items across Price, Storage and Seats. Key highlights: Starter has Price: $0, Storage: 5 GB, Seats: 1; …", with the highest and lowest values of numeric columns (unit-aware). Definition lists ("Key details: Weight: 1.2 kg; …"), bullet lists and numbered lists ("In 4 steps: first, …") are summarized too. Each appears in the teleprompter as a Summarized Table Card. Promotional "Add to cart" tables, layout tables and calendars are left out.
- On-device AI: when Chrome's built-in Summarizer API (Gemini Nano, Chrome 138+) is already downloaded, it writes each section's key points on the device; otherwise, or after a failure or 30 seconds, SiteVocal's own summarizer plays instantly. SiteVocal never starts the model download by itself.
- Optional Turbo Engine (Docs & Lexicon): the user's own Fish Audio key (api.fish.audio/v1/tts, model s2-pro by default) or any OpenAI-compatible speech (/v1/audio/speech) or chat (/v1/chat/completions) endpoint and key, for a neural voice or an LLM-written summary. With no key saved nothing is sent ("0 Bytes Sent to Cloud"); with a key only that endpoint receives the text, without cookies, and the privacy panel names it and counts the bytes.
- Site Briefing mode (deterministic, no LLM, no API): read from the raw page before Readability strips it. Part 1 "What They Do" from JSON-LD Organization / WebSite / SoftwareApplication / Product / LocalBusiness, meta and og:description, and the hero h1 with its lead paragraph ("Site Briefing for [Site] ([domain]). What they are: …"). Part 2 "What They Provide": 3 to 6 feature cards, sections or feature-list items ("What they provide and key capabilities: First, … Second, …"). Part 3 "Pricing & Audience": plan cards and prices, free tiers, trials, open source, "Built for …" ("Pricing and access: …"). Part 4 "Key Takeaways": JSON-LD FAQPage and on-page FAQs, otherwise section takeaways. About 60 to 90 seconds; navigation, headers, footers, forms, buttons, cookie banners, testimonials and call-to-action lines ("Sign up", "Book a demo", "Start free trial") are never read.
- Mode switch: a segmented "Site Briefing (What They Do) | Full Page Read | Summarize Page" pill beside Listen on every page; one click switches and keeps playing, each mode keeps its own place, and the library remembers the choice per page. Root homepages, /pricing and /about pages and marketing landing pages open as a briefing by default; articles open as a full read, with a 45-second overview one click away. The briefing is shown as a dossier sheet (logo, site name, domain, brand-colour swatch, four numbered cards that glow in the site's colour while spoken).
- Web app: double-click index.html, paste any website or article URL into the command bar, press Listen. Quick Try demos: Wikipedia, Paul Graham Essays, Hacker News, Company Homepage (SiteVocal's own product homepage as a Site Briefing, with a built-in snapshot when offline). A segmented control switches between Reader, Library and Docs & Lexicon; the compact address bar appears only once a page is open.
- 3-stage Ad-Shield (runs before Mozilla Readability): stage 1 removes ad slots such as [data-ad], [data-ad-unit], [aria-label*="sponsored" i], .ad-slot, .ad-container, .taboola, .outbrain, .newsletter-signup, .inline-related, .affiliate-disclaimer, and class or id tokens matching (^|[-_\s])(ad|ads|advert|sponsor|promo)([-_\s]|$), so header, read, load and shadow never match; stage 2 removes short "Read more:" / "Related:" link boxes, affiliate disclaimers and newsletter sign-ups; stage 3 reports "Ad-Shield Active · DOM Cleaned · X" in the reader's filter bar. Nodes holding the article are never removed.
- URL mode: the parallel race above, then DOMParser and Mozilla Readability (0.6.0, bundled in vendor/). Wikipedia, Hacker News and GitHub use their official CORS-enabled APIs.
- Chrome extension: download https://github.com/Hotragn/sitevocal and load the folder that contains manifest.json unpacked at chrome://extensions. The toolbar icon or Alt+Shift+S opens the side panel and reads the active tab's live DOM (works on pages the user is logged into). It installs with no site access (activeTab only); "Allow all sites" is optional. Context menus: Read this page, Start SiteVocal From Here (starts at the right-clicked paragraph), Speak Selection, Read linked page. A SPA and infinite-scroll watcher shows a "Page changed · Re-sync" pill without interrupting playback; re-sync keeps the listener's place. With all sites allowed, a URL pasted in the side panel that is already open in a tab is read live from that tab (www., #hash and utm_ parameters ignored), and the side panel reads the active tab as soon as it opens even without a toolbar request. A "Re-read tab" button reads the tab again.
- Filter chips (in a liquid-glass filter bar below the website identity header): Skip Code, Skip Tables, Skip Citations, Smart Lexicon; toggling one rebuilds the script on the same paragraph. With a chip off, code is read line by line, tables row by row and citations announced.
- Smart Lexicon: e.g. → "for example", i.e. → "that is", et al. → "and colleagues", fig. → "figure", emoji runs and markdown noise removed, plus an editable pronunciation dictionary (localStorage key sitevocal_lexicon; defaults SQL → Sequel, arXiv → archive, CLI → C L I, WCAG → W C A G, iOS → i O S).
- Section Outline: h2/h3 headings with per-section listening time; click to jump playback there.
- Clip quote: press B (or the Clip quote pill) to copy the sentence being spoken with its title and URL; clips are kept in the Library tab.
- Up Next queue: queue saved sites or URLs; the next item plays automatically when an article ends.
- Broadcast script (deterministic, no LLM): spoken intro "Welcome to SiteVocal. Now reading from [site]: [title], written by [author]. Estimated listening time: [X] minutes.", section announcements, quote markers and the sign-off "That concludes this article from [site], brought to you by SiteVocal."
- Speech engine: sentence chunks of about 10 seconds, one utterance in flight, cancellation tokens and a watchdog. This fixes Chrome's 15-second speechSynthesis cut-off and prevents overlapping voices when jumping or changing speed (0.75x to 2x).
- Voices: auto-selects the most natural voice for the article language (Natural, Neural, Online, Premium, Siri, Google); manual override; each voice is labelled on-device or online.
- Media Session: lock-screen controls with the site's logo; next and previous track step one sentence.
- Keyboard: Space or K play/pause, J/L previous/next sentence, arrow keys previous/next paragraph, B clip quote, [ and ] speed, 1/2/3 tabs, S sidebar, / command bar or address bar.
- Player: a floating obsidian-glass pill dock (max 760px, centred 20px above the bottom) with the site's logo and title, a burgundy round Play button with previous/next, an emerald waveform and speed/voice pills.
- Honest telemetry: the dock's privacy shield is green ("Local Engine · 0 bytes sent to the cloud") with an on-device voice; with an online voice (Google voices in Chrome, Microsoft Online voices in Edge) it turns amber, says the text is sent to that vendor and offers a one-click "Use on-device voice". The privacy panel also counts words spoken and ads stripped.
- Design: a #F8F9FA canvas with white reading sheets (soft 0 4px 24px elevation), liquid glass only for floating chrome, borderless Saved Library sidebar and Section Outline rail; 15% obsidian (#0B0D0E), 7% emerald (#047857 / #10B981), 3% burgundy (#7A1C24: the Play trigger, the spoken paragraph's 3px rule, the logo's final bar). Reading type: Newsreader 20px / 1.75 in a 66ch column. Website identity header: cover, logo, site-name pill, 36px title, author, listening time. Logo: "The Speaking Tag", a minimal straight-line mark (square frame, 45° code chevron and three sound bars stepping down 9 → 6 → 3, the last one burgundy). Wordmark: mixed-case SiteVocal in Plus Jakarta Sans ExtraBold (800, -0.035em tracking) in obsidian with a burgundy full stop. The start page shows a sound-ripple field of dots that resolve into emerald letters, honouring prefers-reduced-motion, and a "What users reported" switchboard: six common complaints about free read-aloud tools (citations, URLs and tables read aloud; no start-from-here; rewind lands mid-word with no table of contents; SPA pages not re-read; lost place when a popup closes; paywalled citation skipping), each beside the raw text other readers speak and the cleaned line SiteVocal speaks, with a spoken preview.
- Real-world testing: on the 23 article pages with expected text in the newspaper4k test corpus (CNN, TIME, WIRED, CNN Arabic, Nikkei, China Daily and others; 8 languages), SiteVocal's read text has a mean F1 of 96.3% against the expected article text (Mozilla Readability alone: 95.4%), and no URL is read aloud. Right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu) are laid out right-to-left; byline labels in other languages are stripped; meta-refresh redirect stubs are followed.
- Privacy: SiteVocal collects nothing; no backend or analytics; library, queue, clips and dictionary stay in localStorage, and Your data shows and clears them. No remote code: every script is a local file (app.js, vendor/readability.min.js, Tailwind CSS 4.3.3 compiled into vendor/styles.css), and the extension's pages and sandbox run under script-src 'self'. Privacy policy: PRIVACY.md.
- Chrome Web Store: CHROME_STORE_LISTING.md holds the listing texts, the single-purpose statement and the justification of each permission (activeTab, contextMenus, scripting, sidePanel, storage, and the optional host permissions http://*/* and https://*/*).

## Docs

- [README](README.md): features, installation, architecture, Ad-Shield, privacy, browser support and FAQ
- [Web app page](index.html): the studio's HTML, SEO metadata and styles
- [Web app script](app.js): all of SiteVocal's JavaScript (Ad-Shield, extractor, Site Briefing, Summarize Page, speech engine, Turbo Engine, UI)
- [Bundled libraries](vendor/README.md): Mozilla Readability 0.6.0 and Tailwind CSS 4.3.3, with hashes and rebuild steps
- [Privacy policy](PRIVACY.md): what stays on the device and what leaves it, and when
- [Chrome Web Store listing](CHROME_STORE_LISTING.md): descriptions, single purpose, permission justifications
- [Extension manifest](manifest.json): Manifest V3 configuration (side panel, sandbox, permissions, context-menu hook)
- [Content script](content.js): active-tab extraction of content, logos, brand colours, start-from-here anchor and the SPA watcher
- [Context hook](context-hook.js): remembers the right-clicked element for "Start SiteVocal From Here" (registered only with all sites allowed)
